title: Why verification is fast, and what it is not — 11 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Why verification is fast, and what it is not. 11 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/speed.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 10 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 1 is proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 4 pairs; the theorems fall into 8 strands, the largest of 4. Most binding: rounds (3), verifyUs (2). 5 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: ledgerclaims.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 5 files: src/proof/speed.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean, src/proof/ledgerclaims.lean, src/proof/merkle.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 11 sealed receipts fold to 7d92d6c4-dbf8-85d1-bb47-06923a3b753f. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (5, 7, 8, 1, 7, 8, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: demand.lean (5 observed, 0.97 expected, lift 5.18), demand2.lean (3 observed, 1.18 expected, lift 2.54), coin.lean (3 observed, 1.29 expected, lift 2.33). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 3.11 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 4.0% of them — above chance by this measure, though with 33 clusters about 1.65 are expected there by chance alone. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.71; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.58. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 95155bc810f5 (2026-09-15), over 719 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. The structural claim is Merkle's and is credited here as merkle.lean already credits it: a hash tree over n leaves has an O(log n) membership proof, so the inclusion path at each power of two is exactly the exponent. Ralph Merkle, 1979 (thesis); CRYPTO 1987. the_verify_path_is_the_exponent, membership_is_logarithmic_not_linear and the_gap_widens_with_every_doubling RESTATE that property. This file was classified unbounded — "the subject is this deposit's own verification cost" — which was wrong: the cost is logarithmic BECAUSE of a known result, and the repository was already crediting that result three files away. Bounded: what is not prior art is the MEASURED constants on this machine (recompute 21,582,900 µs against a 38 µs walk) and the arithmetic over them. A measurement is not a discovery either, and the file says so. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_verify_path_is_the_exponent — rounds 40 1024 = 10 ∧ rounds 40 16384 = 14 ∧ rounds 40 262144 = 18 ∧ rounds 40 1048576 = 20 record
  2. the_gap_widens_with_every_doubling — 1024 / 10 < 16384 / 14 ∧ 16384 / 14 < 262144 / 18 ∧ 262144 / 18 < 1048576 / 20 record
  3. no_constant_factor_accounts_for_the_gap — ¬ (10000 * 20 ≥ 1048576) ∧ 100 * 10 ≥ 1024 - 24 record
  4. the_measured_ratio_exceeds_the_counted_gap — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun k => 2 ^ k / rounds 40 (2 ^ k) ≤ recomputeUs / verifyUs) ∧ (recomputeUs / verifyUs) * verifyUs ≤ recomputeUs ∧ recomputeUs < (recomputeUs / verifyUs + 1) * verifyUs ∧ recomputeUs / verifyUs = 567971 record
  5. verification_grows_it_is_not_constant — rounds 40 1024 < rounds 40 1048576 ∧ ((List.range' 1 10).all (fun k => rounds 40 (2 ^ k) == k)) record
  6. the_microseconds_return_from_the_nanoseconds_at_every_count — ∀ u : Nat, u * 1000 / 1000 = u record
  7. the_verify_in_nanoseconds_reads_back_its_microseconds — (List.range 1000).all (fun u => u * 1000 / 1000 == u) ∧ nsPerVerify = verifyUs * 1000 ∧ nsPerVerify / 1000 = verifyUs ∧ nsPerVerify > 10000 record
  8. the_advantage_is_the_count_not_the_operation — 1048576 - 20 = 1048556 ∧ 1048576 / 20 = 52428 record
  9. the_break_even_is_the_ratio_of_verifications — 1048576 / 20 = 52428 ∧ 52428 * 20 ≤ 1048576 ∧ 1048576 < 52429 * 20 + 20 record
  10. the_width_is_the_ceiling_of_128_bits_over_the_symbol — (List.range' 1 8).all (fun b => charsFor b * b ≥ 128 && (charsFor b - 1) * b < 128) ∧ charsFor 4 = hexChars ∧ charsFor 6 = hexbitChars ∧ hexbitChars < hexChars ∧ hexbitChars * 100 / hexChars = 68 record
  11. hexbits_are_slower_and_the_ratio_multiplies_back — (List.range' 1 20).all (fun b => (List.range 400).all (fun a => (a / b) * b ≤ a && a < (a / b + 1) * b)) ∧ hexbitMs > hexMs ∧ hexbitMs * 10 / hexMs = 18 record
